quote: do you have a credit score over 670?
stewart_read: Rep runs the credit qualifier exactly per script phrasing, and the customer immediately self-reports below threshold. Per qualifiers.credit_qualifier's spencer_operator_note, stated credit and pulled credit often diverge by 30-50 points across bureaus, so a customer self-reporting sub-670 may still qualify on the bureau Ion actually pulls.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep followed correct, sanctioned procedure if Ion's policy is that setters DQ on stated credit — in that case this is not a coaching gap at all.
coaching_implication: Manager should confirm with Kenny whether setters are meant to DQ on stated credit or pass everyone through to the closer's pull; until resolved, treat this and the resulting exit as a policy question, not automatically a rep error.

quote: Yeah. So our credit kinda got hit a little bit recently.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers that this is a repeat contact with Ion ('I did reach out to you guys couple couple months back') and that a prior rep gave them the 670 threshold. The rep never asks when they last spoke to Ion, who told them this, or logs the return-lead status for follow-up.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this detail as irrelevant once the DQ was clear and prioritized ending the call cleanly — but the schema treats prior contact as free competitive/relationship intelligence regardless of outcome.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always capture prior-contact details (when, who, what was said) into the record before closing out a DQ call, so recycled-lead follow-up has real context instead of a blank file.

quote: Okay. Do do you know anybody that does or that could help?
stewart_read: The customer already disclosed at 00:39 that his wife is also on the title. When credit disqualifies the customer individually, the rep's generic 'know anybody that could help' line misses the concrete, schema-relevant angle of asking whether the co-owner's credit could qualify the household instead.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may not have connected the earlier co-owner answer to the credit question in the moment, which is a reactive miss rather than a deliberate choice to skip it — there's no evidence the rep considered and rejected the co-owner path.
coaching_implication: Train reps to link earlier verify answers (co-owner on title) to later DQ triggers (credit) in real time — asking about the spouse's credit here could have kept the lead alive instead of closing it out.

quote: Okay. Well, then no problem. You can always reach out anytime, and you have a great day.
stewart_read: No callback date, no timeframe, no 'reach back out in X months once your credit clears' — the exit is entirely passive and puts 100% of the burden on the customer to re-initiate.
coaching_implication: Even on a genuine DQ, the rep should own a concrete next step (e.g., 'let's touch base in 3 months' or a scheduled check-in) rather than leaving it open-ended — this protects the recycled-lead pipeline.

quote: It was getting up there pretty high.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers bill-pain language unprompted ('getting up there pretty high') before giving the number — a strong emotional cue the rep could reflect back, but the rep only logs the dollar figure and moves straight to roof type.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have intended to return to the bill-pain emotion after finishing verify items, but the call ends at the credit DQ before any flip occurs, so no evidence supports a deliberate delay.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly acknowledge bill-pain language in the moment ('yeah, that adds up fast') even on short verify calls — it costs seconds and keeps the anchor warm for later use.

stewart_read: Utility name capture is garbled across several fragmented turns (customer says 'Central Mexico Community' then 'Co op' then corrects to 'Central New Mexico?' with the rep supplying 'Community' and 'coop' afterward) — likely a transcription/diarization artifact rather than a coaching-relevant moment, but the section was nonetheless completed.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed; flagged only to note the utility-company capture was functionally completed despite transcript noise.
